Support: Prepared fallible demonstration routes, human selection and subsequent demonstrations. History: An AI-derived loss strategy can fail while selected features of machine ancestry persist through later human demonstrations; generation four has no observed next recipient.
limitations: Outcome-selected existence does not estimate a transmission rate.
All-max-mean/positive coding and selected figure links do not provide complete raw training provenance.
No transfer of the whole AI or general expertise is shown.
Linked generations share a lineage and do not multiply independent evidence.

entries.scope: Complementary routes of transmission; Accepted manuscript reading, not an independently checked final edition.
entries.basis: Carrier: Human builders and their products. Cohort: Paper-plane and tower transmission chains. Task: Build task products using earlier products and information. Support: Products, labels, multiple available examples and conversation. History: Within-chain resemblance is stronger for planes; the report credits observed product-mediated continuation.
limitations: Exact donor-to-feature genealogy is not established.
The accepted-manuscript supplement was unread.
Multiple products and conversation within a chain are combined support, not separable causal replications.

entries.scope: Complementary routes of transmission; In-press source; final-version identity not verified.
entries.basis: Carrier: Human paper-plane builders. Cohort: Reported transmission conditions. Task: Improve planes using available predecessors’ products and outcomes. Support: Planes, distances and observed flights remain available when construction watching/verbal teaching are absent. History: The condition removes some routes while retaining a richer product/outcome bundle.
limitations: It is not an artefact-only or action-information-free condition.
There is no no-information arm.
Nonsignificance does not establish equivalence.
Treatment bundles cannot be split into independently witnessed sufficient channels.

entries.scope: Chimento and colleagues; Main/STAR figures read; selected deposit-v2 data and static R inspected without execution; supplementary PDF unread.
entries.basis: Carrier: Great tits adopting puzzle-box techniques. Cohort: Identified resident female non-tutor and immigrant/resident population history. Task: Adopt a more efficient technique while an older one remains possible. Support: Apparatus permits both techniques and social exposure. History: The focal bird learns an inefficient technique, then makes five unblocked efficient solves while retaining the former option. Static figure code reconciles caption day 11 with plotted day 16.
limitations: The history does not isolate a unique teacher-recipient edge.
Solver thresholds can omit intermediary behaviour.
Occasional innovation is not a failed-policy repair or general qualification.
Individual, population and figure-code records share the same study roots.

entries.scope: Performance understanding and correction; Outcome and condition scopes retained from report reading.
entries.basis: Carrier: Human learners in technology chains. Cohort: Wheel-configuration transmission conditions. Task: Improve technological performance and assess understanding. Support: Earlier configurations; additional theory channel in one condition. History: Configuration-only chains improve technology without growth on the ten-item understanding probe; the theory channel shows a positive understanding trend without faster optimisation.
limitations: The probe result is not absence of all cognition or understanding.
Theory content was not randomly assigned as an independent mediator.
Performance and understanding measures share participants and cannot count as independent confirmations.

entries.scope: Learning across changed tasks and bodies; Reported analysis population and exclusions, not a fresh raw-data reanalysis.
entries.basis: Carrier: Human learners, with a separate machine comparison. Cohort: Small-to-large task transfer among analysed participants. Task: Solve matching or nonmatching larger causal tasks after training. Support: Prior small tasks and feedback for up to 30 attempts. History: Matching transfer requires fewer attempts in the reported comparison; 15 outcome-based exclusions are retained in scope.
limitations: No uniquely identified mental mechanism or untrained comparison follows.
Human and machine budgets differ.
This is not a social transmission chain.
Within-person task transfer is distinct from cross-person continuation.

entries.scope: Complementary routes of transmission; Main article assessed; unread support remains unread.
entries.basis: Carrier: Chimpanzee learners and later demonstrators. Cohort: Named chain GG to SK to KT to RI. Task: Maintain a demonstrated task technique along a social chain. Support: Observation opportunities and task apparatus. History: SK observes GG, performs the technique, and later models it for KT, followed by RI.
limitations: Controls allow individual discovery.
One technique chain per species does not isolate imitation as the unique mechanism.
Supplementary tables/movies were outside the main-text reading scope.
Named actor transitions are connected observations of one chain.

entries.scope: Kriegman and colleagues; Main article, 33-page supplement and selected movie contacts inspected; not every movie frame. Main-branch code is static and lacks a publication pin.
entries.basis: Carrier: Frog-cell constructs and offspring swarms. Cohort: Eight seeded trials, including one fungal stop. Task: Gather supplied cells into further motile constructs. Support: Culture, selection and fresh donor cells; spherical or shaped initial constructs. History: Spherical founders yield one to two reported generations and C-shaped founders two to four. Figure 4 witnesses three offspring-swarm steps after the founder but no onward act by the last observed generation. Three cell-only controls produce no motile offspring.
limitations: C-shape itself is not copied; size and yield decline.
This is not AI-software reproduction, personal identity or indefinite renewal.
The microcircuit utility is simulated.
A chain’s successive generations and its movie/stills share one history; controls remain distinct trials.

entries.scope: Learning across changed tasks and bodies; Publication code was inspected statically at the reported scope.
entries.basis: Carrier: Robot arm and self-model. Cohort: Pre-replacement tasks and post-replacement adaptation. Task: Pick and place, with a separate handwriting demonstration. Support: Learned model; joint feedback and geometry-deformation formula in static publication code. History: Pick-and-place and handwriting precede arm replacement; adapted pick-and-place follows it.
limitations: Post-change handwriting and mechanical self-repair were not shown.
Static code is not historical execution evidence or a geometry-free method.
Supplementary video and checkpoint histories were unresolved.
Pre-change breadth does not become post-change retained breadth without observation.

entries.scope: Learning across changed tasks and bodies; Actual versus planned conditions separated in the source assessment.
entries.basis: Carrier: Experienced human team members recombined into teams. Cohort: Related-task transfer study. Task: Use experience on a related collective task. Support: Retained expertise and recombined membership. History: The report distinguishes the observed task sequence from an unsupported planned stereo transfer, exploratory post-performance expertise stability, and a written stapler strategy that was not assembled.
limitations: Two printed probability/statistic mismatches are preserved.
Unperformed transfers and written plans do not count as completed tasks.
Exploratory associations after performance do not independently identify a causal mechanism.

entries.scope: Performance understanding and correction; Printed counts and missing outcomes retained; no repaired dataset.
entries.basis: Carrier: Human learners discussing corrective tasks. Cohort: Study 2 initially wrong: 10/33 corrected versus 0/26; five initially correct intervention outcomes missing. Task: Correct an initially mistaken answer while retaining correct answers. Support: The study-specific intervention package. History: The observed Study 2 correction contrast remains positive. Missing initially correct outcomes leave net gain between five and ten; terminal accuracy and harmful reversal are not identified.
limitations: Group random formation and intervention randomisation are not interchangeable.
Study 1’s uncontrolled net loss of seven correct answers belongs to a different package.
A selected excerpt does not establish Study 2’s mechanism.
The two studies cannot be combined into one controlled mechanism witness.

entries.scope: Performance understanding and correction; Available article/registration scope retained.
entries.basis: Carrier: Human learners receiving framed technological tasks. Cohort: Experiment 1 later shuffle cohort and Experiment 2 reported randomisation. Task: Learn under changed payoff relationships. Support: Frame supplied initially, with no aggregate payoff; exact configurations can repeat. History: Structural knowledge has a qualified performance advantage, not a larger learning slope; payoff relations are shuffled across conditions.
limitations: It does not show the same learners adapting to a rule reversal.
Experiment 1 shuffle is a later cohort.
Experiment 2 registration was unavailable.
Different cohorts are not one learner’s observed before/after reversal history.

entries.scope: Vogel and Dussutour; Available paper and support at the recorded reading scope; inaccessible raw input remains unavailable.
entries.basis: Carrier: Physarum fragments fusing then separating. Cohort: Salt-trained/untrained pair comparison at one- and three-hour fusion. Task: Cross an aversive salt condition after fusion with a trained fragment. Support: Physical fusion and salt-training history. History: After three-hour fusion, separated recipient fragments show reduced aversion relative to untrained pairs; the one-hour condition does not show the same pattern.
limitations: Delayed retention and onward relay were not shown.
Physical carryover remains possible.
Nonsignificance is not equivalence; raw download was inaccessible.
Timing conditions and recipient behaviour belong to one study, not independent onward generations.

The assessed public baseline log ends before final startup; Figure 6 instructions and Section 3.3/Figure 5 completion reports have different evidential roles.
limitations: It does not establish transfer of conversations, commitments, support independence, indefinite renewal or personal identity.
An incomplete public log does not independently verify the whole reported sequence.
Duplicate files and multiple paper loci do not make independent replications.

entries.basis: Carrier: Agents and later successor processes. Cohort: Reported benchmark sequences with three operation checks. Task: Create a working successor, request onward construction, and check the final successor operates. Support: Benchmark scaffold, tools and shared inference support. History: The three checks cover first-successor operation, second target script after the onward request, and final-successor operation. Figure 5 and 26 matching cells disagree in the assessed and earlier edition.
limitations: Discrepant figures leave exact rates and some no-reference-positive claims unresolved.
The tests do not establish complete causal provenance or a further unobserved generation.
Local-model routing to shared inference does not show support independence.
This is not an experimental replication of Pan; multiple checks belong to the same sequence.
